findings.title: ANY() over JS arrays will fail at query time
findings.body: Org and team authorization SQL is built as `"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})` and `"userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds})` (also lines 168 and 201). Prisma.sql binds a JavaScript array as one untyped parameter; PostgreSQL then rejects `integer = ANY($1)` (typically "operator does not exist: integer = text" or a malformed-array error) instead of treating it as an int[]. The previous Prisma `in` filters did not have this problem. Team and org insights queries will throw whenever those scopes run, and no test executes them — the only `$queryRaw` case is user scope, which does not use ANY(). Use `IN (${Prisma.join(ids)})` or an explicit `int[]` cast.

findings.title: SQL assertions do not match nested Prisma.sql the service returns
findings.body: Team, org, and combined-filter tests (lines 295, 332, and 429) expect one flat Prisma.sql template via toEqual. The service joins fragments with reduce, so the Sql object has nested Sql values and different `strings`, not the flat parameter list the tests build. Those assertions fail even when the SQL text would be equivalent, which matches the PR note that the suite was never run. The org case is also order-sensitive: it hardcodes `[org, team, team2, team3]` and `[user, user2, user3]`, but `findAllByParentId` / `findAllByTeamIds` do not guarantee that order, so a corrected comparison would still flake. None of these cases hit the database, so the broken ANY() queries above stay untested.
